blocks.text: Condo buildings in Cape Horn
Debut — 1251 Ghuman Place (Beedie Living)

The first Fraser Mills tower: a 36-storey concrete condo high-rise with 318 homes, approved by Council on September 25 (developer source), on a five-storey podium holding 32 townhomes at the base, on a site preloaded to stand 20 feet above median sea level because it is on the Fraser River floodplain. A later developer article records Debut as sold out. Completion timing conflicts between sources: the developer's approval article expected move-in by 2026, current listings record the year built as 2027, and the developer's Chapter article expects Debut, Encore and Chapter all complete by 2028. REDMA applies to developer contracts.
Encore — 53 Kong Court (Beedie Living)

The second Fraser Mills tower: 32 storeys, 306 homes of condominiums and three-bedroom stacked townhomes, concrete construction, built to Energy Step Code 3, with almost 27,000 sq ft of amenities (developer sources). A presale source states the project is in the Cape Horn district of Coquitlam and expects completion in the summer of 2028; one current listing records the year built as 2029 — the conflict is noted, not resolved. REDMA applies.
Chapter — 58 Kong Street (Beedie Living)

The third Fraser Mills building and the developer's only wood-frame complex on the site: two six-storey low-rises over a shared parkade, 173 suites in total (82 units in the northern building, 91 in the southern), stratified housing, expected complete in 2028 (developer source). A presale-directory record for the same address records 173 units, 6 floors, low-rise form and preconstruction status. REDMA applies.

items.t: Where the condo stock concentrates: there is no completed apartment-condo stock on the slope itself. The only strata product filed under Cape Horn by listing sources is the Fraser Mills presale site below the slope, on the Fraser River waterfront at United Boulevard & King Edward Street (Debut, Encore and Chapter by Beedie Living), plus one older townhome complex on Cape Horn Avenue itself (Crescentview).
SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: Coquitlam condos & townhomes median was $625,000 in September 2026 ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days on market).

The City's own permit record underlines the slope's form: the 2022 development statistics for Cape Horn (planning areas 15 and 16) record 18 net residential units created that year (36 created, 18 demolished), all in single-family / secondary-suite / carriage-house form, with no townhouse or apartment units.
Transit anchors: the nearest SkyTrain stations are Braid, Lougheed Town Centre and Burquitlam — none is inside the sub-area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Cape Horn

items.t: Floodplain — the Fraser Mills diligence item: the Debut site is preloaded to stand 20 feet above median sea level because it is on the Fraser River floodplain — flood construction level, strata insurance and deductible position are first-order questions for every Fraser Mills purchase. On the slope, the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse, and Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks while s.523 covers riparian areas.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cape Horn condos

items.t: Coquitlam replaced its OCP in 2026. The City adopted an Interim Official Community Plan on April 27, 2026, streamlining the old Citywide OCP (Bylaw No. 3479, 2001), with a fuller OCP update anticipated to begin in 2027. Planning documents and listing copy citing the old Citywide OCP designations are already a plan out of date.

The sub-area's attached listings are a construction site, not a resale market. Cape Horn's 13 condos & townhomes listings in September 2026 sit against a City permit record (2022, planning areas 15/16) of zero townhouse or apartment units created — the listings are Fraser Mills presale contracts at three buildings (Debut 318 homes, Encore 306, Chapter 173) that between them will add 797 homes below the slope.

A 12-kilometre water main is being built through the area. Metro Vancouver's Coquitlam Water Main Cape Horn Section is approximately four kilometres long and 2.2 metres in diameter, running to Hickey Drive and Mariner Way, including a trenchless tunnel crossing under Lougheed Highway — construction disruption on the Mariner Way corridor is a live diligence item for slope addresses.

Debut's podium hides the townhouses. Of Debut's 318 strata units, 286 are high-rise apartments and 32 are townhouses inside the five-storey podium — "townhomes at Debut" are podium units in a tower strata, not a townhouse complex.

Chapter is marketed to seniors but is not published as 55+. The developer describes Chapter's buyers as families upgrading or seniors downsizing. In BC only a 55+ bylaw under SPA ss.123.1/123.2 can restrict age — marketing language cannot.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Cape Horn

items.t: There is no completed strata townhouse complex in Cape Horn, so there is no resale Form B to pull for townhouse stock on the slope. When a strata complex does apply (Strata Property Act s. 59), the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. At Fraser Mills, presale diligence is the developer's disclosure statement, not a Form B — do not let a sales centre present the two as equivalents.

Flood and watercourse — the two diligence items by location: at Fraser Mills, the Debut site is preloaded to stand 20 feet above median sea level because it is on the Fraser River floodplain — flood construction level, strata insurance and deductible position are first-order questions for every Fraser Mills purchase. On the slope, the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse, and Zoning Bylaw s. 519 sets flood protection setbacks from watercourses while s. 523 covers riparian areas.

Coquitlam property taxes and utilities: property tax payment was due July 2, 2026 for the January 1 – December 31, 2026 year, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance of current taxes after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after September 15, 2026 (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants).

Infrastructure note for slope addresses: Metro Vancouver is constructing the Coquitlam Water Main — approximately 12 kilometres in four sections; the Cape Horn Section is approximately four kilometres long and 2.2 metres in diameter, running from Westwood Street and Dewdney Trunk Road to Hickey Drive and Mariner Way, including a trenchless tunnel crossing under Lougheed Highway — construction disruption on the Mariner Way corridor is a live diligence item.

Of Debut's 318 strata units, 286 are high-rise apartments and 32 are townhouses inside the five-storey podium — "townhomes at Debut" are podium units in a tower strata, with a tower strata's fees, insurance and depreciation profile, not a townhouse complex's.

faq.a: Strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Short-term rentals are a separate question a bylaw can still restrict.

Debut's 32 podium homes and Encore's stacked homes are the project's townhouse-form product, inside the towers.

faq.a: Inside the towers, not beside them: Debut's five-storey podium holds 32 townhomes at the base of a 36-storey tower (286 of its 318 units are apartments), and Encore's 306 homes mix condominiums with three-bedroom stacked townhomes. Chapter is low-rise apartments, not townhouses. All are presale components — none is a standalone townhouse complex.
